claims.text: A16Z predicts 90% of code will be written by AI by 2026
Software engineer job postings are up 18% YoY despite AI coding tools
AI code generation accuracy drops to 34% on tasks requiring >3 file changes
Autonomous AI agents fail on 73% of real production debugging tasks

hook_variants.text: AI will write 90% of code by 2026, says a16z. Meanwhile, engineering job postings are up 18% YoY. Someone is wrong.
hook_variants.reasoning: Creates immediate contradiction. Reader must resolve the tension.

hook_variants.text: 34%. That's how accurate AI code generation is when a task requires touching more than 3 files.
hook_variants.reasoning: Surprising statistic directly from research. Creates credibility and tension.

draft_iteration_1.text: The AI will replace software engineers narrative is the most confidently wrong prediction in tech right now. Here's the data they're ignoring:
A16Z says 90% of code will be written by AI by 2026. Bold claim. But engineering job postings are up 18% YoY — even as Copilot, Cursor, and Devin have all shipped.

critique_iteration_1.rewrite_instructions: Tweet 1: 'narrative' is a cliché in tech writing. Replace with the specific data upfront. Try the counterintuitive hook: '90% of code written by AI by 2026 — that's the a16z prediction. Engineering job postings are up 18% YoY. Someone is confidently wrong.' Voice match: the person's examples show they open with numbers, not with meta-commentary about narratives.

draft_iteration_2.text: AI will write 90% of code by 2026, says a16z. Meanwhile, engineering job postings are up 18% YoY. Someone is wrong. It's a16z. Here's why:

The 90% claim assumes AI can handle production-grade complexity. The data says otherwise. AI code generation accuracy drops to 34% when a task requires changing more than 3 files. Most real bugs require touching 5-10.
Devin, the most hyped autonomous coding agent, fails on 73% of real production debugging tasks. Not toy benchmarks. Real repos. Real bugs.

Why the gap between the hype and the data? a16z is measuring token generation speed. Engineering is measured in system comprehension — understanding 200k lines of context, implicit contracts, deployment risk.
AI is genuinely transforming how engineers work. The 10x developer is real — but it's a human engineer using AI tools, not an AI replacing the engineer.

The job postings number is the tell. Companies are hiring more engineers because AI reduces the cost of shipping — which expands what's worth building, which creates more demand for engineers who can think about systems.
If you're a founder: hire engineers who use AI. Don't replace engineers with AI. The ones who understand both will build circles around the teams who picked a side.
What's your read — will the 10x developer model hold for the next 5 years, or is there an inflection point we're not seeing yet?
